  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type

          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time

          readOnly: true

      required:
        - type

        - timestamp

## Summary

I implemented the registration-date rule for `POST /api/owners`: when no registration date is supplied, it defaults to the server's current date, and `registrationDate` is returned in ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` format (a supplied date is preserved).

Changes made:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added an optional `registrationDate` property (`type: string, format: date`) to the `OwnerFields` schema. Because `Owner` extends `OwnerFields`, this makes the field both accepted on create and returned on read. The OpenAPI generator maps `format: date` → `java.time.LocalDate`, which Jackson serializes as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

2. **`Owner.java`** (entity) — added a `registrationDate` `LocalDate` field mapped to a `registration_date DATE` column, with getter/setter and the `LocalDate` import.

3. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — after mapping the DTO, defaults `registrationDate` to `LocalDate.now()` when it is `null`. MapStruct auto-maps the field by name in both directions (request→entity and entity→response), so a supplied value flows through unchanged.

4. **Schema files** (`hsqldb`, `h2`, `mysql`, `postgres`) — added the `registration_date DATE` column to the `owners` table.

5. **`hsqldb/data.sql`** — the seed inserts used positional `INSERT INTO owners VALUES (...)`, which broke once a column was added; I gave them an explicit column list so the new nullable column is skipped. (The `h2` and `postgres` seeds already used explicit column lists, so they needed no change.)

Note: the JDBC repository implementation (`JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl`) isn't on the active `spring-data-jpa` path used at runtime or in tests, so it was left unchanged.

I implemented the registration-date rule for `POST /api/owners`: when no registration date is supplied, it defaults to the server's current date, and `registrationDate` is returned in ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` format (a supplied date is preserved).

Changes made:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added an optional `registrationDate` property (`type: string, format: date`) to the `OwnerFields` schema. Because `Owner` extends `OwnerFields`, this makes the field both accepted on create and returned on read. The OpenAPI generator maps `format: date` → `java.time.LocalDate`, which Jackson serializes as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

2. **`Owner.java`** (entity) — added a `registrationDate` `LocalDate` field mapped to a `registration_date DATE` column, with getter/setter and the `LocalDate` import.

3. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — after mapping the DTO, defaults `registrationDate` to `LocalDate.now()` when it is `null`. MapStruct auto-maps the field by name in both directions (request→entity and entity→response), so a supplied value flows through unchanged.

4. **Schema files** (`hsqldb`, `h2`, `mysql`, `postgres`) — added the `registration_date DATE` column to the `owners` table.

5. **`hsqldb/data.sql`** — the seed inserts used positional `INSERT INTO owners VALUES (...)`, which broke once a column was added; I gave them an explicit column list so the new nullable column is skipped. (The `h2` and `postgres` seeds already used explicit column lists, so they needed no change.)

Note: the JDBC repository implementation (`JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl`) isn't on the active `spring-data-jpa` path used at runtime or in tests, so it was left unchanged.
